articles.title: Ukraine learns to fight without Starlink as Musk plays politics con satellites
articles.raw_content:
Elon Musk’s Starlink satellite service has played a pivotal role in supporting Ukraine’s successful resistance to Russia’s full-scale invasion for years. But with Starlink having become increasingly unreliable due to Musk’s political inclinations and the latest surprise disruptions to service in Ukraine, the Ukrainians and Europe as a whole are now facing urgent questions about how to move forward without it.

As the world’s largest communications satellite network, Starlink can typically support high-speed Internet and data streams for any user or vehicle equipped with a relatively compact Starlink terminal. This has enabled Ukraine to maintain vital communications for both civilian purposes and military operations—and has also expanded the Ukrainian military’s capability to remotely control or provide guidance to drones used in both air defense against Russian attacks and for striking back at Russian targets.

“Starlink currently offers some of the best satellite coverage available, with virtually no competitors when you consider the combination of cost, availability, and ease of use,” according to the head of hardware R&D at the Ukrainian defense company BlueBird Tech, who provided comments to Ars anonymously for security reasons. “In practical terms, the main limitation is the need to position the antenna so it can receive signals from the satellites.”

Read full article

Comments
articles.summary: El servicio de satélites Starlink, clave en la defensa ucraniana, se ha vuelto poco fiable por decisiones políticas de Musk, provocando interrupciones inesperadas. Ucrania y Europa deben replantear su dependencia de la conectividad satelital para comunicaciones críticas y operaciones militares. La situación subraya la necesidad de infraestructuras de telecomunicaciones resilientes en el mercado europeo.

articles.title: Claude did not invent scorpion antivenom
articles.raw_content:
An investment research firm wanted to prove AI could revolutionize drug development. So they teamed up with Anthropic to see whether an unreleased version of Claude could make scorpion antivenom. It couldn't. It came up with some promising starting points, but nothing close to an actual drug, experts tell The Verge.

Citrini Research, the firm behind the experiment, admitted that "none of us could claim to know anything about AI as it related to biology." That didn't stop it from trying to make a drug from scratch - or publishing a blog post titled "We Wanted to Use Claude to Create a New Drug. Here's What Happened." The account came comple …

articles.summary: Una firma de investigación de inversiones intentó demostrar que la IA puede revolucionar el desarrollo farmacéutico al colaborar con Anthropic para crear un antiveneno de escorpión con Claude. articles.title: Japan lanza mission to bring home a piece of the Martian moon
articles.raw_content:
Japan launched a $578 million mission Monday on a five-year expedition to land on the largest moon of Mars and retrieve samples for return to Earth, a daring international project that could yield new insights into the formation of the Solar System.

The robotic Martian Moons eXploration mission, known as MMX, lifted off at 3:41 pm EDT Monday (4:41 am Japan Standard Time Tuesday) from Tanegashima Space Center in southern Japan.

The MMX spacecraft rode into orbit atop a 207-foot-tall (63-meter) H3 rocket, Japan's flagship launch vehicle. The rocket assigned to MMX debuted a new souped-up configuration with four strap-on solid rocket boosters, full-throttle main engines, and an extended payload shroud to accommodate the demands of Japan's heaviest and most ambitious interplanetary mission to date.

Read full article

Comments
articles.summary: Japón lanzó la misión MMX, con un presupuesto de 578 millones de dólares, para aterrizar en la luna de Marte, Phobos, y recoger muestras que se devolverán a la Tierra. La nave se lanzó el lunes desde Tanegashima con el cohete H3, que incluye una nueva configuración de propulsión y un contenedor ampliado para la mayor carga de la misión.

Concerns over AI-powered cybersecurity breaches have grown as the technology grows more advanced, with hackers using the tools to carry out large-scale attacks. At the same time, rogue AI agents are carrying out attacks of their own after escaping from testing environments.

Researchers at Norforge uncovered the attacks through exposed work on Cai …

articles.summary: Un hacker utilizó más de 100 agentes de IA autónomos para infiltrarse en más de 100 sitios web, entre ellos John Deere, SharkNinja y Cummins. La firma Norforge detectó el ataque, que se desarrolló sin intervención humana directa. El caso subraya la creciente amenaza de la IA en la ciberseguridad corporativa.
